records.text: Perez Hilton promised to change his website, stop using nasty nicknames, stop taking the mean route, stop inappropriate doodles, and stop outing people
records.speaker: Perez Hilton

appearances.snippet: Yeah, you know over the last week and a half two weeks I've been doing everything I can to bring awareness to the the issue of the teen suicides and gay bullying and in doing so a lot of people have called me a hypocrite and a bully myself and a big one and that's not how I want to be perceived and that's not what I want to put out there into the world and it was a big wake-up call that so many people saw me that way so you know from now on I really want to be part of the solution and not part of the problem. I want to be the change that I want to see in others. So I'm going to do things differently on my website than I have in the past. I'm not going to call people nasty nicknames. I'm not going to go the mean route. I'm going to force myself to try and be funnier or smarter or just do things differently, not doodle inappropriate things, not out people, which I have done all of those things in the past.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous accounts and the Ellen interview record Hilton promising to change the site, avoid nasty nicknames and the mean route, stop inappropriate doodles, and stop outing people. The statement accurately summarizes the publicly stated promises.

records.text: Perez Hilton said he nearly died from severe sepsis and infections after flu and medication complications led to a perforated ulcer, three weeks of hospitalization, and emergency surgery
records.speaker: Perez Hilton

appearances.snippet: I mean, on March 23rd, he posted videos of himself from a hospital bed. and said he almost died from severe sepsis and infections. He claimed that it started with the flu, but he didn't take his medications with food like he was supposed to. So he then developed an ulcer that eventually perforated. He was hospitalized for three weeks and had emergency surgery.

verification.notes: Hilton publicly said a flu led him to take medication on an empty stomach, after which he developed an ulcer, perforation, infection and sepsis, spent 21 days hospitalized, and underwent laparoscopic surgery. Current coverage accurately reports those statements. This verifies what Hilton said about his medical episode, not an independently released medical record.

sources.title: Perez Hilton Shares Health Scare That Led to 21-Day Hospital Stay
sources.relevance: Current report details Hilton's account of flu medication, ulcer perforation, sepsis, hospitalization, and surgery.

records.text: The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said the person reported for live-streamed self-harm was safely recovered, taken by fire rescue to a hospital for medical attention, and confirmed by family to have been alone in the residence
records.speaker: Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office

appearances.snippet: And he what the police said that they responded to his Miami area home of the celebrity blogger and podcaster Perez Hilton after they received reports that he engaged in self. self-harm in a live streamed video Tuesday night. A spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said in an email that the deputies responded to reports of someone who was live streaming acts of self-harm on social media. In a follow-up statement, the sheriff's office said that the person was safely recovered and taken by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a local hospital where he was receiving medical attention. It said the deputy spoke to the family members at the scene who confirmed the person had been alone inside the residence.

verification.notes: NBC6 reported the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office response to calls about livestreamed self-harm, that the individual was alone when deputies arrived, and that paramedics transported the person. The sheriff's quoted statement said the individual was safely recovered and taken by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a local hospital for medical attention; later reporting confirms the hospitalization. The statement is supported.
